title: Japan Considers New Tax on Electric Cars from 2028
paragraphs: The Japanese government is looking at introducing a new tax on electric vehicles and plug-in hybrids starting in May 2028, according to Kyodo News.

The tax would be added to the vehicle weight tax that drivers already pay during regular car inspections. The amount would depend on the car's weight, and people with plug-in hybrids would likely pay about half as much as those with all-electric vehicles.
Only about 3% of cars sold in Japan are electric, while in China that number is around 33%, and in Europe it's 22%.
So why introduce a new tax on these vehicles?

The goal is to make sure all drivers help cover the cost of maintaining roads. Drivers of gasoline cars already help pay for this through taxes on gas, while those with electric cars use the same roads without paying these taxes.
Electric cars are also often heavier than similar gasoline cars because of their large batteries, meaning they cause more damage to roads.
The government has yet to decide how much the new tax will be. However, automakers have called for a delay, saying that the tax could make Japanese drivers even less likely to choose an electric car.
However, there are signs that more people in Japan are interested in buying electric cars.

On November 20, for example, the government closed applications for subsidies for electric and other environmentally friendly vehicles because sales were higher than predicted and money was running low, according to Kyodo News.
Plans for next year's subsidies are yet to be decided.
